descriptor: A smoky-grey cat of the high Asian mountains, balanced by a thick tail almost as long as its body.

range.summary: Rugged mountains of 12 Central and South Asian countries, mostly between 3,000 and 5,500 m, with about 60% of the range in China.

source.label: Snow Leopard Survival Strategy 2014 (GSLEP), compiling Fox 1989 and 1994, McCarthy et al. 2003, Jackson et al. 2010

population.note: Each point is the midpoint of a published expert range, not a census, and the differences mostly reflect better information rather than real change. Less than 2% of the range has been surveyed rigorously; IUCN estimates 2,710 to 3,386 mature individuals.

threats.title: Retaliatory killing
threats.detail: Herders kill cats that take sheep, goats and yaks from poorly protected corrals.

threats.title: Poaching and illegal trade
threats.detail: Pelts and bones are traded across the region, often from cats caught in snares.

threats.title: Prey decline
threats.detail: Overgrazing and hunting reduce the blue sheep and ibex that snow leopards depend on.

threats.title: Climate change
threats.detail: A rising treeline could swallow up to 30% of Himalayan snow leopard habitat.

threats.title: Mining and infrastructure
threats.detail: Roads, mines and border development fragment remote mountain habitat.

places.name: Hemis National Park (Rumbak valley)
places.note: Ladakh's best-known snow leopard site, tracked with local spotters and homestays.

places.name: Kibber, Spiti Valley
places.note: High desert valleys where cats hunt ibex and blue sheep near the village.

places.name: Shey Phoksundo National Park
places.note: Remote trans-Himalayan park in Dolpo, demanding but wild.

sightings.tip: In deep winter snow pushes ibex and blue sheep to lower slopes and the cats follow, while February and March are the mating season, when they move and call more.

actions.title: Choose responsible cashmere
actions.detail: Overgrazing by cashmere goats strips the pastures wild prey need, so look for certified sustainable fibre.

actions.title: Back predator-proof corrals
actions.detail: Secured night pens and livestock insurance stop the losses that lead to retaliatory killing.

actions.title: Never buy pelts or bones
actions.detail: Any purchase keeps the poaching and trafficking networks profitable.

actions.title: Stay in community homestays
actions.detail: Tourism income that reaches herder families makes a live cat worth more than a dead one.
